newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - APRIL 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - APRIL 4.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The international community yesterday sent a message of support to Albania's government that it would bolster efforts to restore normality and that Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino was the man to talk to. In Tirana, Albanian President Sali Berisha continued to undermine the efforts of the national unity government led by Fino.

--With the beginning of talks within the ruling party PASOK on issues of social insurance and labour relations, old divisions have once again come to the fore. A number of leading PASOK cadres distanced themselves from recent comments by Prime Minister Costas Simitis on the future of the job market.

--Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos set three clear conditions for talks with Ankara yesterday: the complete withdrawal of threats of war by the Turkish prime minister or foreign minister; discussions on the legal framework to govern the Aegean; and a mechanism to resolve conflict.
--The government has woken up to the serious drug problem facing the country's youth and will announce measures next week, following the third drug death in as many days.

--Seven retail firms will face prosecution over irregularities in the sale of goods to credit card holders. The development ministry, in cooperation with the Association of Greek Banks, is moving ahead with measures to restore transparency to credit card transactions.
--Defence Minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos implied recently that he may consider standing for the post of president of ruling party PASOK at the next congress.

--A recent decision by an Athens court to award compensation of 16.5 million drachmas to a property owner who claimed damages from the state's changes to town planning legislation has opened the floodgates to any citizen to claim against the state's changes in legislation.

--TV personality Liana Kanelli is preparing a "Rock on the Rocks" concert on the uninhabited islet of Imia - focus of a dispute between Greece and Turkey last year that brought the two close to war - for late in May. Kanellis says she has requested the Kalmynos Coast Guard to issue visas to Turks wanting to attend the sun-up to sun-down party. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
